attribute-control-chart.name: Control Chart (Attribute)
attribute-control-chart.description: SPC charts for count data: p, np, c, u
attribute-control-chart.whenToUse: Control-chart counted data: p and np for defectives, c and u for defects, with Nelson-type rules on the plotted points.

bar.name: Bar Chart
bar.description: Bar chart from worksheet columns: frequency, mean, or sum per category
bar.whenToUse: Compare counts or values across categories, optionally split or stacked by a group.

boxplot.name: Boxplot
boxplot.whenToUse: Compare the spread, median and outliers of one or more numeric columns, optionally split by a group.

chart-suggestion.name: Chart Suggestion
chart-suggestion.description: Proposes suitable chart types for the selected columns
chart-suggestion.whenToUse: You have columns of a worksheet and need to know which chart fits their roles — a ranked list with a preview, from which the chosen chart opens as a module of its own.

contour-plot.name: Contour Plot
contour-plot.description: Visualize response surfaces z = f(x, y) as contour diagrams
contour-plot.whenToUse: Draw the response surface of a two-factor model as contour lines — from polynomial coefficients or an own formula in x and y — optionally with measured points.

data-import.name: Data Import
data-import.description: Read data from third-party formats (Minitab .mpx, CSV/TSV/TXT, Excel/ODS, JSON/NDJSON, Q-DAS AQDEF) into a worksheet
data-import.whenToUse: When data from a third-party source is to be brought into a data collection; for an agent from CSV or JSON text, with profiles for common measuring-machine exports.

distribution-fit.name: Distribution Fit
distribution-fit.description: Fit data to multiple distributions and rank by Goodness-of-Fit test
distribution-fit.whenToUse: When it is unclear which distribution describes a measured characteristic: fits normal, lognormal, Weibull, exponential and further distributions to one numeric column and ranks them by goodness of fit; requires at least 5 values.

dmaic-calendar.name: Calendar
dmaic-calendar.description: Project calendar: appointments per phase in a month and a week view
dmaic-calendar.whenToUse: When the appointments of a project should be kept — meetings, measurement windows, deadlines —, each assigned to a phase and shown in a month or week view; not for tasks without a fixed point in time, that is what the todo list is for, and not for planning activity durations and dependencies.

doe-planner.name: DoE Planner
doe-planner.description: Design of Experiments: Full Factorial, Fractional, Plackett-Burman, CCD, Box-Behnken, Taguchi
doe-planner.whenToUse: When the effect of several factors on one or more responses is to be studied in a planned experiment: full or fractional factorial, Plackett-Burman, response surface (CCD, Box-Behnken), Taguchi or optimal (D, A, G), also as an EVOP project over several phases. Which design type fits is settled beforehand in the DoE advisor (doe-advisor).

heatmap.name: Heatmap
heatmap.description: Cross-tabulation as a color-coded grid — cell color shows frequency, mean, or sum per (X, G) combination.
heatmap.whenToUse: Show a value or a count for every combination of two categories as a colour grid — e.g. cycle time per shift and line.

histogram.name: Histogram
histogram.description: Frequency distribution with boxplot and statistics
histogram.whenToUse: Show the distribution of one or more numeric columns as frequency bars, with summary statistics and a confidence interval.

hypothesis-test.name: Hypothesis Test
hypothesis-test.description: Variance and mean tests with automatic normality assessment and power analysis
hypothesis-test.whenToUse: When you need to decide whether an observed difference in location or spread goes beyond the noise — one mean against a target value, two samples against each other, or k groups together. Requires metric data in a data collection.

individual-value-plot.name: Individual Value Plot
individual-value-plot.description: Plot every individual observation per group as a point
individual-value-plot.whenToUse: Show every single value of one or more numeric columns, grouped by up to three categories, with mean and confidence interval per group.

ishikawa.name: Ishikawa 6M
ishikawa.description: Root cause analysis with 6M categories and expert scoring
ishikawa.whenToUse: When possible causes of a problem are to be collected, ordered by 6M and rated by the team, so that the most likely ones get tested with experiments; states can be kept as snapshots and compared. For a single chain of causes by asking why, use 5-Why.

morphological-box.name: Morphological Box
morphological-box.description: Combine solution concepts from parameters and options, check incompatibilities
morphological-box.whenToUse: When a solution consists of several sub-functions and alternative whole concepts should be combined systematically — not for scoring or choosing the concepts, that belongs to solution selection.

mosaic.name: Mosaic Plot
mosaic.description: Visualises the joint distribution of two categorical variables — column widths show the marginal frequency, segment heights show the conditional shares.
mosaic.whenToUse: Compare how two categorical variables combine: column widths show the share of each x category, segment heights the share of each group within it.

msa-typ2.name: MSA Type 2/3 (Gage R&R)
msa-typ2.description: Measurement System Analysis Type 2 (with operator, Gage R&R) and Type 3 (no operator, automated measurement systems)
msa-typ2.whenToUse: When a measurement system with several parts (and usually several appraisers) should be assessed: a crossed study gives repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) by ANOVA; without an operator column the module computes as type 3 for automated measurement systems — not for the capability of a single gage on a standard, which type 1 covers. Requires parts, optionally appraisers, and the measurements as columns of a data collection.

msa-typ5.name: MSA Type 5 (attribute)
msa-typ5.description: Attribute Measurement System Analysis — multiple appraisers, kappa-based agreement (Cohen, Fleiss, weighted)
msa-typ5.whenToUse: When an attribute measurement system (good/bad, classes, ordinal levels) is to be assessed: several appraisers rate parts, repeatedly, against an optional reference. The result is kappa agreement, effectiveness and a verdict by AIAG or Bosch rules — not for measured characteristics, which types 1 to 3 cover. Requires a data collection with a part column and either an appraiser and a rating column (long layout) or one rating column per appraiser and trial (wide layout).

multi-vari.name: Multi-Vari Chart
multi-vari.description: Stages single measurements across up to four factors and splits the spread into variance components — shows where the variation actually comes from.
multi-vari.whenToUse: When the spread of a measured characteristic must be traced to its sources: stages every single measurement by two to four factors (for example shift, cavity, part) and splits the variance into components, nested or crossed, by ANOVA or REML; needs one numeric measurement column and two factor columns.

opportunity-flowchart.name: Opportunity Flowchart
opportunity-flowchart.description: Two-column flow: value-added steps versus rework
opportunity-flowchart.whenToUse: When an existing chain needs sorting into value-added work versus rework — not for capturing a new process without that distinction yet.

outlier-test.name: Outlier Test
outlier-test.description: Run classical outlier tests (Grubbs, Dixon Q, Generalized ESD, Tukey IQR, Hampel, Z-Score) in parallel on a column
outlier-test.whenToUse: When a measured characteristic may contain outliers: tests one numeric column with up to seven methods (Grubbs, Dixon Q, generalized ESD, Tukey IQR, Hampel, Z-score, modified Z-score) and reports which values each method flags; requires at least 3 numeric values.

pareto.name: Pareto Chart
pareto.description: Bar chart sorted by descending value with a cumulative-percentage line — the classic "vital few" tool.
pareto.whenToUse: Rank categories by frequency or by a summed value to find the vital few — with a cumulative percentage line.

pie-chart.name: Pie Chart
pie-chart.whenToUse: Show how a total splits into parts: one slice per distinct value, or per label with the values summed.

probability-plot.name: Probability Plot
probability-plot.description: Normal probability plot for checking normality, with optional grouping
probability-plot.whenToUse: Check whether one or more numeric columns follow a distribution: points on the straight line mean a good fit.

process-capability.name: Process Capability
process-capability.description: Process Capability Analysis — Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk, PPM, Sigma Level
process-capability.whenToUse: When it must be shown how well a process keeps a measured characteristic inside its specification limits: Cp and Cpk (short term, from the within-subgroup spread), Pp and Ppk (long term), PPM and sigma level, with confidence intervals. Works with one-sided or two-sided limits, individual values or subgroups. Needs at least one limit (lower or upper) and at least 2 numeric values from a data collection column or from loaded example data.

project-charter.name: Project Charter
project-charter.description: Project mandate: problem statement and measurable goals
project-charter.whenToUse: At the start of a project, to record the problem, measurable goals and the project organisation — the basis every later phase refers to.

resampling.name: Resampling
resampling.description: Bootstrap confidence intervals and permutation tests for one, two, paired and k samples
resampling.whenToUse: When a statistic of one, two, paired or k samples needs a confidence interval or a test without assuming a distribution: bootstraps the interval (BCa or percentile) and tests by permutation (two samples, paired, k groups) or against a target value (one sample). Each sample needs at least 2 numeric values (10 for Ppk).

run-chart.name: Run Chart
run-chart.description: Median run chart with four runs tests
run-chart.whenToUse: Look at a series over time for non-random patterns — clustering, mixtures, trends, oscillation — before building control limits.

sipoc.name: SIPOC
sipoc.whenToUse: When the boundaries of a process need clarifying — who supplies, what goes in, which steps run, what comes out and who receives it; not for the flow itself with its decisions and branches, which is what a flowchart is for.

survey-builder.name: Survey builder
survey-builder.description: Create VoC questionnaires, send them as HTML, import and evaluate the answers
survey-builder.whenToUse: When customers or stakeholders are to be surveyed in writing: design the questionnaire, send it as an HTML file per recipient, read in the answer files and evaluate them — without a server, the data stays in the project.

triz-function-analysis.name: Function Analysis (TRIZ)
triz-function-analysis.description: Components, interactions and function model – the starting point for the other TRIZ tools
triz-function-analysis.whenToUse: When a technical system is to be broken down component by component to find harmful, insufficient and excessive functions and to spot trimming candidates by value and cost — not for a contradiction that is already named; the contradiction matrix and the physical contradiction cover that.

worksheet.name: Data Collection
worksheet.description: Spreadsheet for data entry and management
worksheet.whenToUse: The shared data substrate: measurements land here before an analysing tool reads them through a column reference. Almost every analysis starts with a data collection.

xy-plot.name: XY Plot
xy-plot.description: Create scatter plots from worksheet columns
xy-plot.whenToUse: Show the relationship between two numeric columns as a scatter plot, optionally grouped or as bubbles sized by a third column.
